San Bernardino County, California, recently passed an ordinance relating to off road vehicles (County ordinance No. 1590, Sec. 2, Title 2, Division 8, Chapter 4, of San Bernardino County Code, dated 8 September, 1970). We requested an opinion on the effect of this ordinance as related to mineral prospecting and exploration from a highly regarded legal firm. To quote from the reply:
"The general mining laws provide that the public domain is open to entry for the purpose of prospecting, developing and mining, and thus those engaged in these activities may cross the surface. As a consequence, a motor vehicle engaged in prospecting, etc., may cross the surface.
"However, such permitted surface use, without the benefit of a permit from the Bureau of Land Management should not and would not include the operation of recreational vehicles such as dune buggies, motor cycles and the like."
Any restriction on ORV that does not allow for the working use of such vehicles would effectively prevent mineral exploration over large areas of the public domain, despite the fact that such areas may be legally open to mineral entry. The days when a grizzled prospector, leading a burro can discover valuable surface outcrops are long since gone. To explore for minerals today requires the use of sophisticated geophysical equipment that cannot be transported by burro or backpack. In some cases, a general area of possible geologic interest can be outlined by the use of such equipment mounted in aircraft, but more thorough investigation can only be done on the ground.
We do not question, and in fact support, regulations that will control the unrestricted use of amusement vehicles, but we strongly protest any implementation that does not allow for the economic and technical considerations required by the Act of 1969, and feel that mineral exploration should be considered as a vitally necessary exception on all public lands open for mineral entry.
Respectfully submitted,
Hon. Harrison Loesch
Mgr, Pacific Southwest Regional Office Robert
Mgr, Mid-Continent Regional Office
